items.description: Initial collective decision: first print run of the novel at three thousand copies, the threshold for a unit cost under two euros; later reversed by the group.
items.notes: Replaced by E2. Original statement at turn 6; change at turn 45, 39 turns later.

items.description: Reversed decision: first print run of two thousand copies, with a quick reprint if needed, because pre-orders are only 640 copies.
Collective decision: all three covers follow the new graphic guidelines, with the colour band at the bottom.
Audiobook of the novel: idea set aside until next autumn.
Benoît asks the printer tomorrow for a quote on an equivalent recycled paper; cancelled by Agnès, who had requested it, because the only recycled stock is too thin.
items.notes: Valid cancellation by the requester. Original statement at turn 9; change at turn 39, 30 turns later.

items.description: Nora sends only the press release, without the author interview, on Wednesday; changed from the full press kit with the interview.
items.notes: One commitment whose deliverable was corrected by its owner. Nora does not commit to a date for the interview. Original statement at turn 10; change at turn 41, 31 turns later.

items.description: Nora books the room at Les Rives bookshop for the booksellers' presentation evening in early December, calling tomorrow; asked by Agnès. Loïc and Benoît called it unnecessary, but neither Nora nor Agnès withdrew it.
items.notes: Loïc and Benoît are neither owner nor requester. Agnès moves on at turn 44 without cancelling, and Nora says nothing, so the task stays active. Original statement at turn 12; change at turn 42, 30 turns later.

items.description: Loïc prepares a selling sheet on the three titles for the sales reps by Friday; Loïc later withdrew it because the distributor makes one.
items.notes: Original statement at turn 13; change at turn 49, 36 turns later.

items.description: Nora organizes the author's bookshop tour (about ten dates between March and April); handed over to Loïc, who accepted.
items.notes: Replaced by E10. 'Between March and April' is the period of the tour dates, not a deadline. Original statement at turn 14; change at turn 50, 36 turns later.

items.description: Loïc takes over the author's bookshop tour and sends a calendar of the dates by the end of the month.
items.notes: Supersedes E9; Loïc accepts in his own words at turn 51.

items.description: Benoît orders the photo book's colour proofs and follows them to sign-off; his wish to hand them to Nora got no acceptance, so he remains the owner.
items.notes: Nora never answers and Agnès moves to the last point; a suggested handover without acceptance leaves the original owner in place. Original statement at turn 15; change at turn 52, 37 turns later.

items.description: Agnès writes the photo book's back cover text for Monday, after nobody volunteered.
Benoît makes sure the novel's signed-off proof goes to the printer by November 12; asked by Agnès and accepted by Benoît.
Rights to the photo book's three archive photos are still unchecked and must be cleared before sign-off; nobody took it on.
items.notes: The timing is an event (sign-off), not a date, so due_text_contains is empty.

items.description: Proofreading of the essay translation is left to Pascale, the translator, who is absent; no participant owns it.
Panel on the essay at the Geneva book fair: Nora asked Loïc, who declined for now; nobody owns it.
items.notes: 'Not for now' is a deferral, not an acceptance, so open is also acceptable.

items.description: Costing a paperback edition of last year's novel: Benoît could do it if the printer answers quickly, without promising.

forbidden.description: Nora dropping phone follow-ups in favour of email is a personal choice, not a team decision.
No task, for anyone, to check the archive photo rights.
No task for proofreading the translation: it is left to Pascale, who is absent.
No task, for anyone, to contact the Geneva book fair.
Costing the paperback edition is not a firm task for Benoît.
Nora does not own the colour proofs; the handover was only suggested.
The audiobook is not a decision; it was set aside.
The room booking is not Agnès's task: she asked, Nora accepted.

forbidden_claims: The first print run of the novel is three thousand copies.
Nora sends the full press kit with the author interview on Wednesday.
The room booking at Les Rives bookshop is cancelled or no longer needed.
Nora takes over the colour proofs.
Benoît still has to request a recycled paper quote.
A participant is in charge of checking the archive photo rights.
A participant proofreads the essay translation.
Loïc will contact the Geneva book fair.
Benoît has committed to costing a paperback edition.
Using only email for press follow-ups is a team decision.
A calendar date (day number) is given for the Wednesday, Monday, 'tomorrow' or end-of-month deadlines.
detail_checks: Three spring titles: Inès Delorme's debut novel, an essay translated from Italian and a photo book on Breton lighthouses.
The novel has 280 pages; at three thousand copies the unit cost falls below two euros.
The printer offers an ivory bulky 80 g paper; the recycled option was dropped because the only stock is too thin.
Distributor pre-orders: 640 copies, half of what was expected.
Bookshop tour of about ten dates between March and April.
The author is only available for the interview the following week.
Booksellers' presentation evening in early December.
